text:
ana: Heads up — noticing a perf regression after the recent probe changes when we detect GPU capabilities on the new SM90 hosts. Baseline throughput down ~18% for seq512 across our standard fp16 kernel paths.

josh: Can you paste the probe output and the kernel route decision?

ana: Sure — here's the probe snippet from boot logs:

```
[hw-probe] device=nv0 sm=90 driver=537 features=[tensor_core:true bf16:false fp8:unknown]
[cap-detect] prefers_tc_kernel=true prefer_bf16=false fallback_path=kernels/v2/tc_fallback
[route] chosen_path=kernels/v2/tc_fallback seq_threshold=256
```

ana: And a microbench result (seq=512, batch=8):

```
kernel: tc_fastpath throughput=850 tok/s latency=12.1ms
kernel: tc_fallback throughput=700 tok/s latency=15.6ms
kernel: reference_fp16 throughput=1020 tok/s latency=9.8ms
```

maria: Wait, why is prefer_bf16=false on SM90? The hw probe should enable bf16 for SM90+ unless driver hides it.

dmitri: We have a known driver quirk where /proc/capabilities reports BF16=false until a specific CUDA init sequence runs. CIbot used in upstream tests had to call cudaDevicePreference or similar. Could be race at startup.

ana: Repro steps: cold boot, start inference runtime immediately, run a small load test. Warm starts show correct bf16=true and route to reference_fp16/tc_fastpath with expected perf. Cold starts consistently prefer tc_fallback.

josh: Any kernel selection logs from the runtime? Even just the pick reason would help.

ana: Attached excerpt from our route_decisions.log:

```
TS=1715804310 device=nv0 pick_reason=cap_probe:bf16=false -> choose tc_fallback
TS=1715804315 device=nv0 probe_retry=1 cap_probe:bf16=true -> choose tc_fastpath
TS=1715804325 request_id=... routed_to=tc_fallback (sticky until probe success)
```

maria: That sticky state is the issue. We set a hysteresis to avoid oscillation but it seems we're being too conservative and penalizing cold-starts. Should consider a probe_retry window + fallback grace that rechecks after Xs.

dmitri: Agreed. Two proposals: (1) defer final kernel choice until after async cudaInit completes (adds ~200ms startup), or (2) allow transient optimistic re-evaluation after N requests or Y ms. My vote: (2) — keep latency low but allow re-eval quickly.

josh: +1 for (2). Also we need a quick mitigation: if reference_fp16 microbench > tc_fallback by >20% for same seq/batch, prefer moving to reference path even if BF16 probe is false. We already have perf history per model.

ana: I can draft a change: add a bootstrap_reprobe window of 5s where a lightweight microbench (1-2 inferences) runs in background to validate kernel choice, and if perf delta >15% switch. If microbench fails, keep current behavior.

maria: Make sure to gate that behind a feature flag and add a max extra memory budget so we don't OOM on tiny hosts. Also log metrics: reprobe_count, reprobe_latency, reprobe_result.

devops-bot: Deploy note: rolling 10% of SM90 fleet with reprobe=true for 24h, healthcheck threshold: 10% throughput delta.

josh: Also add a telemetry event when probe reports fp8/unknown so we can triage driver gaps.

ana: I'll open a PR with the stubbed reprobe + feature flag + metric names. Will include repro test harness that cold boots a container and asserts route stabilizes to the higher-throughput kernel within 5s.

maria: Thanks — also link to the device-quirks doc from infra (driver-init quirks) in the PR so reviewers know the background.

dmitri: TL;DR: cold-start probe race toggles bf16 flag -> sticky fallback path -> perf regression for seq512. Short-term: reprobe window + quick microbench. Long-term: coordinate with driver/infra to ensure bf16 accurate at probe time.

ana: Filing the PR now. Ping me for review. :rocket:
